items.title: Chuck Israels interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 11, 2021
items.q: Red Mitchell was the virtuoso who made all of us look silly. He was really superb.

ctx.x: Right. And he said, “Chuck Israels is a superb technician who handles the double bass as easily as if it were a guitar. He’s one of the reasons why musicians have come away reeling from performances by the Bill Evans Trio in a mood poised between elation and utter despair.”

Well he gives me too much credit for virtuosity. Well too much — it’s how he saw it. It was his perception of it. And maybe the perception of some other people. From my perspective, knowing my limitations in terms of virtuosity and technical prowess I think I used my abilities efficiently and perhaps — and I was a lot faster than I am now too, but that’s just — that’s true. I was fast enough for the music. And faster than, but mostly it was melodic, a melodic perspective about what you could do on the bass. I…
I want to go back to your composing and arranging for a bit. And can you describe where inspiration comes from? How does something new get started?
